question: During the Basic Control Skills test exercises, which four categories will the examiner score you on?
choice_a: Pull-ups, encroachments, looks, and final position
choice_b: Speed, mirror checks, signal use, and braking force
choice_c: Fuel efficiency, gear selection, horn use, and parking brake timing
choice_d: Steering smoothness, seat position, mirror adjustment, and door checks
explanation: The manual states that during the Basic Control Skills test exercises, you will be scored for pull-ups, encroachments, looks, and final position.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring

question: According to the manual, what is a "pull-up" during a backing exercise?
choice_a: Pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position
choice_b: Stopping the vehicle without changing direction
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Sounding the horn before starting the exercise
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as pulling forward on a backing exercise to clear an encroachment or to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring - Pull-ups

question: What does the manual define as an "encroachment" during a Basic Control Skills exercise?
choice_a: Crossing over or touching an exercise boundary line or cone with any portion of your vehicle (other than mirrors at door mirror height or higher)
choice_b: Pulling forward to correct your position
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check your position
choice_d: Sounding the horn at the end of an exercise
explanation: The manual states that crossing over or touching exercise boundary lines or cones with any portion of your vehicle, other than the vehicle's mirrors or other unique vehicle parts at door mirror height or higher, is scored as an encroachment.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring - Encroachments

question: How many free pull-ups are you allowed on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and how many on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: One (1) free pull-up on Exercise 2 and two (2) free pull-ups on Exercise 4
choice_b: Two (2) free pull-ups on Exercise 2 and one (1) free pull-up on Exercise 4
choice_c: Unlimited free pull-ups on both exercises
choice_d: Zero free pull-ups on either exercise
explanation: The manual states you are allowed one (1) free pull-up on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and two (2) free pull-ups on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Exercise 2 and Exercise 4

question: How many free "looks" (safe exits to check vehicle position) are permitted on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing, and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing?
choice_a: A maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 and two (2) free looks on Exercise 4
choice_b: A maximum of two (2) free looks on Exercise 2 and one (1) free look on Exercise 4
choice_c: Three (3) free looks on each exercise
choice_d: No free looks are allowed on either exercise
explanation: The manual states you may be allowed a maximum of one (1) free look on Exercise 2 - Straight-line Backing, and two (2) free looks on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, to check the position of your vehicle.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring - Looks

question: The manual states you will be scored for final vehicle position on which two exercises?
choice_a: Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Exercise 1 - Forward Stop and Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing
choice_d: All four exercises equally
explanation: The manual specifies that final position is scored on Exercise 2 - Straight-Line Backing and on Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring - Final Position

question: When you are permitted to exit the vehicle during a backing exercise to check its position, what must you do first?
choice_a: Set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral
choice_b: Turn off the engine completely
choice_c: Sound the horn twice
choice_d: Activate the four-way flashers
explanation: The manual instructs that before exiting the vehicle to check its position, you must set the parking brake(s) and place the vehicle in neutral, then safely exit/enter by facing the vehicle and maintaining three (3) points of contact at all times.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Scoring - Looks

question: What may result in an automatic failure for an unsafe act during the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while the vehicle is in motion
choice_b: Requesting clarification from the examiner about the instructions
choice_c: Taking a free pull-up you are entitled to
choice_d: Sounding the horn at the end of an exercise
explanation: The manual states that committing an "unsafe act," such as forgetting to set the parking brake or opening the door while in motion, may result in an automatic failure and the test may be terminated by the examiner.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Failure to Follow Instructions or Unsafe Act

question: What is the correct order of the four exercises in the Basic Control Skills test?
choice_a: Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Reverse Offset Backing
choice_b: Straight-Line Backing, Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Offset Tracking
choice_c: Reverse Offset Backing, Forward Offset Tracking, Forward Stop, Straight-Line Backing
choice_d: Forward Offset Tracking, Forward Stop, Reverse Offset Backing, Straight-Line Backing
explanation: The manual lists the four exercises in order: Step 1 - Forward Stop, Step 2 - Straight-Line Backing, Step 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, and Step 4 - Reverse Offset Backing.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Basic Control Skills Test

question: During Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, how many times may you stop while driving forward through the alley?
choice_a: Only once, which is then judged as your final position
choice_b: As many times as needed to line up the vehicle
choice_c: Exactly twice
choice_d: You may not stop at all until reaching the end of the alley
explanation: The manual states that for Exercise 1 - Forward Stop, you drive forward through the alley and stop with the front most part of the vehicle within the box; you may stop only once, which is then judged as your final position.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Exercise 1 - Forward Stop

question: During Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, what is prohibited?
choice_a: Back-ups, stopping, or exiting the vehicle
choice_b: Using turn signals
choice_c: Shifting gears
choice_d: Checking mirrors
explanation: The manual states that during Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking, there are NO back-ups or stopping allowed, and you are NOT permitted to exit the vehicle during this exercise.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Exercise 3 - Forward Offset Tracking

question: During Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, the rear most part of your vehicle must come to rest within a box of what size at the end of the alley?
choice_a: A three (3) foot box
choice_b: A ten (10) foot box
choice_c: A one (1) foot box
choice_d: A twenty (20) foot box
explanation: The manual states that for Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing, you must bring the rear most part of your vehicle within the three (3) foot box at the rear of the alley, and the vehicle must be straight within the alley when completed.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Exercise 4 - Reverse Offset Backing

question: What must you do before you can proceed to the Road Test?
choice_a: Pass the Basic Control Skills test
choice_b: Complete the pre-trip vehicle inspection test only
choice_c: Pay an additional testing fee
choice_d: Complete the Road Test first, then the Basic Control Skills test
explanation: The manual states that the Basic Control Skills test must be passed before you can proceed to the Road Test.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 12 - Basic Control Skills, Road Test

question: During the on-road driving test, which of the following is a requirement you must meet at all times?
choice_a: Wear your safety belt
choice_b: Use the horn at every intersection
choice_c: Keep the radio off
choice_d: Drive at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic conditions
explanation: The manual states that at all times during the test you must drive in a safe and responsible manner, wear your safety belt, obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws, and complete the test without an accident or moving violation.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: If your test route does not have certain traffic situations, what may the examiner ask you to do?
choice_a: Simulate a traffic situation by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing
choice_b: Automatically fail that portion of the test
choice_c: Skip that portion of the test with no substitute
choice_d: Reschedule the test entirely
explanation: The manual explains that if the test route does not have certain traffic situations, you may be asked to simulate one by telling the examiner what you are or would be doing if you were in that traffic situation.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13 - On-road Driving, How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, unsafe coasting occurs when your vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for how long while slowing for a turn?
choice_a: More than the length of your vehicle
choice_b: More than 30 seconds
choice_c: More than 100 feet
choice_d: At any time whatsoever
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as occurring when your vehicle is out of gear for more than the length of your vehicle while slowing down for a turn.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: If you are stopping behind another vehicle during the on-road test, where should you stop to maintain a safe gap?
choice_a: Where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you
choice_b: As close as possible to the vehicle ahead
choice_c: At least one full block behind the vehicle ahead
choice_d: Anywhere, as long as you come to a complete stop
explanation: The manual instructs that if stopping behind another vehicle, you should stop where you can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead of you, which represents a safe gap.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.1 - Turns

question: While driving through an intersection during the on-road test, what must you avoid doing?
choice_a: Changing lanes while proceeding through the intersection
choice_b: Checking traffic thoroughly in all directions
choice_c: Yielding to pedestrians and traffic in the intersection
choice_d: Keeping your hands on the wheel
explanation: The manual states that when driving through an intersection, you must not change lanes while proceeding through the intersection, but must check traffic thoroughly, decelerate and yield to pedestrians and traffic, and keep your hands on the wheel.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: As you approach an intersection, what must you do regarding coasting if you need to stop?
choice_a: Come to a complete stop with no coasting, maintaining a safe gap behind any vehicle in front of you
choice_b: Coast up to the stop line to conserve momentum
choice_c: Coast through if no other vehicles are visible
choice_d: Slow to a rolling stop only
explanation: The manual specifies that as you approach an intersection, if necessary, you must come to a complete stop (no coasting) behind any stop signs, signals, sidewalks, or stop lines, maintaining a safe gap, and your vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.2 - Intersections

question: During the Urban Business portion of the on-road test, where should your vehicle be positioned, and how should your speed compare to traffic?
choice_a: Centered in the right-most lane, keeping up with the flow of traffic but not exceeding the posted speed limit
choice_b: Centered in the left-most lane, exceeding the flow of traffic when safe
choice_c: Straddling two lanes to prepare for a lane change
choice_d: As close to the center line as possible, matching the fastest vehicle on the road
explanation: The manual states that during Urban Business driving, your vehicle should be centered in the proper lane (right-most lane), and you should keep up with the flow of traffic but not exceed the posted speed limit.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.3 - Urban Business

question: Before entering the expressway during the on-road test, what should you do?
choice_a: Check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane
choice_b: Accelerate to maximum speed before merging
choice_c: Stop at the on-ramp until all traffic clears completely
choice_d: Enter without signaling to avoid confusing other drivers
explanation: The manual instructs that before entering the expressway, you should check traffic, use proper signals, and merge smoothly into the proper lane of traffic.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.5 - Expressway or Rural/Limited Access Highway

question: During the Stop/Start maneuver, once your vehicle is stopped, what should you do with the parking brake and gear shift?
choice_a: Apply the parking brake and move the gear shift to neutral or park
choice_b: Leave the parking brake off and keep the vehicle in gear
choice_c: Apply the parking brake but keep your foot on the clutch
choice_d: Shift into reverse and apply the parking brake
explanation: The manual states that once stopped for the Stop/Start maneuver, you must activate your four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, move the gear shift to neutral or park, and remove your feet from the brake and clutch pedals.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the Stop/Start maneuver after releasing the parking brake, what must you NOT do before the vehicle begins to move?
choice_a: Turn the steering wheel
choice_b: Check traffic in all directions
choice_c: Turn off the four-way flashers
choice_d: Activate the left turn signal
explanation: The manual instructs that when resuming, you should release the parking brake and pull straight ahead, and you must not turn the wheel before your vehicle moves.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.6 - Stop/Start

question: When approaching a curve during the on-road test, what should you do before entering it?
choice_a: Reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_b: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_c: Shift into neutral to coast through the curve
choice_d: Brake heavily while turning the steering wheel
explanation: The manual states that before entering a curve, you should reduce speed so that further braking or shifting is not required in the curve, and you should keep the vehicle in the lane while continuing to check traffic.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.7 - Curve

question: While any part of your vehicle is in a railroad crossing, what must you NOT do?
choice_a: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
choice_b: Keep your hands on the steering wheel
choice_c: Continue moving forward at a steady speed
choice_d: Look and listen for trains before reaching the crossing
explanation: The manual states that all commercial drivers must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of their vehicle is in the crossing.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: If you are driving a bus, school bus, or a vehicle displaying placards, the manual requires you to stop at a railroad crossing within how many feet, but not less than how many feet, from the nearest rail?
choice_a: Within 50 feet, but not less than 15 feet
choice_b: Within 100 feet, but not less than 25 feet
choice_c: Within 25 feet, but not less than 5 feet
choice_d: Within 15 feet, but not less than 5 feet
explanation: The manual states that a driver of a bus, school bus, or vehicle displaying placards must stop the vehicle within 50 feet but not less than 15 feet from the nearest rail.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: As a bus, school bus, or placarded vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, when should the four-way flashers be activated and deactivated?
choice_a: Activated as the vehicle approaches the crossing and deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks
choice_b: Activated only while the vehicle is stopped and deactivated before moving
choice_c: Never activated at a railroad crossing
choice_d: Activated only if a train is visible
explanation: The manual states that as the vehicle approaches a railroad crossing, activate the four-way flashers, and the four-way flashers should be deactivated after the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.8 - Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the on-road test, what might the examiner ask you to identify?
choice_a: The posted clearance or height
choice_b: The posted weight limit
choice_c: The speed limit under the overpass
choice_d: The name of the overpass
explanation: The manual states that after driving under an overpass, you may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after going over a bridge, you may be asked about the posted weight limit.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.9 - Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: For a School Bus endorsement, the manual requires the school bus to come to a complete stop how far away from students at the stop before student discharge begins?
choice_a: At least 10 feet away
choice_b: At least 25 feet away
choice_c: At least 5 feet away
choice_d: At least 50 feet away
explanation: The manual states that as you stop for the student discharge, you must bring the school bus to a complete stop at least 10 feet away from students at the stop, place the transmission in neutral/park, set the parking brake, and activate the stop arm and red warning lights.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: As a school bus approaches a student pick up, what warning lights and signal must be activated?
choice_a: Amber warning lights and the right turn signal
choice_b: Only the hazard flashers
choice_c: Red warning lights and the left turn signal
choice_d: High beam headlights
explanation: The manual states that as you approach the student pick up, you must decelerate, continue checking traffic, activate amber warning lights and right turn signals, and move as far as possible to the right on the traveled portion of the roadway.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.10 - Student Discharge (School Bus)

question: Regarding clutch usage on a manual transmission vehicle, which practice does the manual warn against?
choice_a: Riding the clutch to control speed, coasting with the clutch depressed, or "popping" the clutch
choice_b: Always using the clutch to shift
choice_c: Double-clutching when shifting
choice_d: Avoiding revving or lugging the engine
explanation: The manual states that under Clutch Usage, you should always use the clutch to shift and must double-clutch when shifting, but you must not ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.11(a) - Clutch Usage

question: Under the Gear Usage general driving behavior category, when should you avoid shifting gears?
choice_a: In turns and intersections
choice_b: On straight, empty roads
choice_c: While on the expressway
choice_d: While approaching a stop sign well in advance
explanation: The manual states that under Gear Usage, you should not grind or clash gears, should select a gear that does not rev or lug the engine, and should not shift in turns and intersections.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.12(b) - Gear Usage

question: Under the Brake Usage general driving behavior category, how should you apply the brakes?
choice_a: Smoothly, using steady pressure, without riding or pumping the brake
choice_b: By pumping the brake repeatedly for better control
choice_c: By riding the brake lightly at all times for readiness
choice_d: As harshly as possible in all stopping situations
explanation: The manual states that under Brake Usage, you should not ride or pump the brake and should not brake harshly, but instead brake smoothly using steady pressure.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.13(c) - Brake Usage

question: Under the Lane Usage category, on a multiple lane road, in which lane should you finish a left turn?
choice_a: The lane directly to the right of the center line
choice_b: The right-most (curb) lane
choice_c: Any lane that is open
choice_d: The lane farthest from the center line
explanation: The manual states that under Lane Usage, you should complete a turn in the proper lane on a multiple lane road, finishing a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line, and finishing a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.14(d) - Lane Usage

question: Under the Steering general driving behavior category, when may you take a hand off the steering wheel?
choice_a: Only while shifting, and both hands must return to the wheel once the shift is complete
choice_b: At any time while driving in a straight line
choice_c: Only while checking mirrors
choice_d: Never, under any circumstances
explanation: The manual states that under Steering, you should not over or under steer the vehicle, and must keep both hands on the steering wheel at all times unless shifting; once you have completed the shift, return both hands to the steering wheel.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.15 - Steering

topic: On-Road Driving Test - Use of Turn Signals
question: Under the Use of Turn Signals category, when should you cancel your turn signal?
choice_a: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_b: Only when the examiner instructs you to
choice_c: Before beginning the turn
choice_d: Turn signals should never be cancelled manually
explanation: The manual states that you should use turn signals properly, activate them when required and at appropriate times, and cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Idaho Commercial Driver's License Manual (2022 CDL Testing System, July 2026 Edition), Idaho Transportation Department Division of Motor Vehicles, Section 13.1.17 - Use of Turn Signals
